title: Universal simulation of coded machines
statement: For every bit string $\alpha$, there is a constant $C\in\mathbb{N}$ such that for every bit string $x$, both of the following hold: if the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes an output $y$ from $x$ within $t$ steps, then the universal machine computes $y$ from the paired encoding of $\alpha$ and $x$ within $C(t+1)$ steps; and if the universal machine computes some output $y$ from that paired encoding within some finite number of steps, then the machine decoded from $\alpha$ computes $y$ from $x$ within some finite number of steps.
hypotheses_covered: there exists a natural-number constant $C$ uniform over all inputs $x$
forward simulation for every output and time bound $t$
reverse simulation for every output when the universal computation halts within some time
